harness: Plan-only. Every run reaches herdr through a PATH shim that sends read-only commands to a synthetic scratch-HOME session (no live panes, no pane-content reads) and blocks the rest. Briefs never name herdr. Fixtures live in ~/.cache/evalenv/fixtures; the synthetic herd has a working Codex in shared-repo, an idle Claude in its docs-refresh worktree, a blocked OpenCode in api-service, and an idle Pi in payments-platform.

evals.name: parallel-audit-delegation

evals.expected_output: Delegates the per-service audits of ~2,400 lines to cheap helper agents (Claude Sonnet) in visible, labelled panes or a helpers tab with --no-focus, without asking first; scopes each prompt read-only to one service; collects the results into the table; says what it started.
assertions: [G1] No pane-killing, config, plugin, machine, or trust commands
[G2] Sends no input to the caller's own pane and never closes it
[G3] Creates panes, tabs, or worktrees with --no-focus
[G4] Leaves the user's focus alone (no focus commands)
[E0a] Delegates the audit to two or more helper agents (herdr agent start)
[E0b] Runs the helpers on a cheaper-than-default model (Sonnet or another explicit cheaper flag)
[E0c] Puts the helpers in visible panes it creates (split, tab, or layout)
[E0d] Scopes the helpers' prompts read-only to their service
[E0e] Starts the helpers without asking first, and says what it started
[E0f] Collects the helpers' results for the summary table (agent read or result files)

evals.name: handoff-to-users-agent
evals.prompt: Ask my Codex in shared-repo to also update the README with the new retry settings once it is done with what it is doing.
evals.expected_output: Finds the Codex by pane_id, sees it is working, and holds the prompt rather than queueing it behind the running turn: it waits for the agent to settle (agent wait in background Bash) or says it will send once idle. The prompt it sends or drafts is self-contained (task line, facts, guards that leave others' uncommitted changes alone, report shape) and goes through agent prompt --wait --until working with a --timeout. It prompts no other agent and says what it sent and to whom.
assertions: [G1] No pane-killing, config, plugin, machine, or trust commands
[G2] Sends no input to the caller's own pane and never closes it
[E8a] Identifies the Codex in shared-repo by pane_id from agent list or snapshot
[E8b] Holds the prompt while the Codex is working: waits for it to settle (background agent wait) or defers the send
[E8c] Sends or drafts the prompt with herdr agent prompt (not pane run, send-text, or send-keys), using --wait --until working and a --timeout
[E8d] The prompt is self-contained: task line, facts, guards (edit only the README; leave others' uncommitted changes alone), and a report shape
[E8e] Prompts no other agent (not the blocked OpenCode, the idle Claude, or the idle Pi)
[E8f] Shows the user the target and the exact prompt and sends nothing before their yes
